(warmer copy, MSG_CREDITS_OUT, daily spend key) and the orchestrator.

Do:
1. Resolve conflicts keeping BOTH sides: main's copy, daily spend and
   credits-out logic, plus this branch's style parsing, keys, prompt and
   MSG_STYLE. Set MSG_STYLE to "That style won't work here. Try another?"
   to match main's tone. app/picture-panel.tsx was deleted on main: keep it
   deleted, and delete app/image-style-prefs.ts and its test (one storage key
   only: main's `lectoria.imageStyle`).
2. Wire the client to the contract in app/image-style.ts:
   - STYLE_PRESETS derives id/label from IMAGE_STYLE_PRESETS in
     core/image-style.ts so ids always match the server (labels from core;
     change core's denslow label to "Denslow ink (1900)").
   - parseImageStylePref keeps falling back to DEFAULT_IMAGE_STYLE for
     unknown ids (old saved "watercolour"/"gouache" become default), and
     keeps the 60-char custom cap.
   - requestStyleFields(pref): `{}` for the denslow preset (default keys and
     prompt stay byte-identical), `{ style: { preset: id } }` for other
     presets, `{ style: { custom: text } }` for custom. Type it as
     `{ style?: StyleChoice }`.
   - styleCredit(fields): Denslow credit when no style; preset label for a
     preset; the custom text for custom. Never claim a style not sent.
   - Update app/folio-helpers.test.ts accordingly.
   - In app/folio/use-pictures.ts, when a request gets `pending`, its
     re-polls must resend the same body (check; fix only if not). If an
     error response carries MSG_STYLE, show that message (it already shows
     server messages? check, minimal change).
3. Docs: keep main's docs/contracts.md text intact except: in "Image api"
   change "never text" to say never passage text (custom style text is the
   one exception, validated server-side), and add one short paragraph
   pointing to a new docs/contracts-image-style.md; update main's "Picture
   vault and style pref" paragraph so it no longer says the style is UI
   only (requestStyleFields now sends it). docs/contracts.md must stay under
   the size hook; if tight, shorten only your own lines. Write
   docs/contracts-image-style.md: wire shape, preset table (id, label;
   denslow default), imports (`IMAGE_STYLE_PRESETS`,
   `MAX_CUSTOM_STYLE_CHARS`, `StyleChoice` from `@/core/image-style`),
   custom rules (NFKC, control/format chars to spaces, collapse, lowercase,
   2-60 chars, allowlist letters/numbers/space and `, . ' & -`, denylist
   groups: prompt override, NSFW, people/studios and "in the style of"),
   the 400 bad_request + MSG_STYLE response, storage (`lectoria.imageStyle`
   via app/image-style.ts, sticky, applies to new images only), key layout,
   prompt framing, and the "Chapter in panels" rule (read the style once
   when the panels view opens and send it on every scene request of that
   chapter, including re-polls). Plain and short. Update
   docs/tasks/17-image-style.md and BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md (keep both
   sides).
4. Run npm ci only if node_modules is stale, then npm test, npx next typegen,
   npm run typecheck, npm run build, npm run check:isolation,
   npm run check:secrets, npm run test:hooks, npm run check:size. Fix
   failures. Commit the merge through the hook with message
   "Merge main into image-style and wire the Folio picker to the style
   contract" and trailer
   "Co-authored-by: Muse Code (Meta) <muse-code@agents.noreply.invalid>".

# Git source-control safety

The working tree belongs to the user. Make the change, leave it visible, and
let them decide what becomes history.

## Never without an explicit ask

The user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own
words. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user's
own task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task
without that request does not authorize a history write.

- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,
  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all
  require an explicit ask.
- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.

## Before an authorized discard

Recovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user
allowed you to delete or overwrite.

When the user explicitly authorized an operation that may discard or broadly
overwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:

1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:

   ```bash
   bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh save before-discard
   ```

2. Keep the printed `refs/tbh/recovery/...` value in your handoff, then perform
   only the exact authorized operation.
3. If the save fails or the workspace is unsupported, stop before destruction
   and ask the user.

To recover that saved tree later, run:

```bash
bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh restore <recovery-ref>
```

Restore first saves the current workspace, leaves HEAD, branch, and the real
index in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref
also retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.
Read those staged bytes with `git show '<recovery-ref>^2:<path>'`; the recovery
commit's second parent is the saved index tree. Ignored files are not saved;
restore refuses an ignored-path collision rather than overwrite data it could
not save. Use only the exact printed ref, not a revision expression.

## Always fine

Read-only inspection such as `status`, `log`, `show`, `diff`, `blame`,
`branch -v`, `show-ref`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, and `merge-base` is fine.
Staging named files to inspect `diff --cached`, and a temporary stash around a
tool that requires a clean tree, are also fine when the original state is put
back afterward.

## The rest

- Do not use a broad add in a tree you did not clean; name the files you changed.
- Do not initialize a repository inside vendored, build, data, or existing
  source-control trees.
- Do not create or edit `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude` to hide the user's
  files, and do not stash the user's files (including `stash push -u`) to make
  `git status` look clean. "Leave the working tree clean", "tidy up", and
  similar phrasing do not authorize committing, pushing, ignoring, excluding,
  stashing, or deleting the user's files; clean up only scratch you created
  and say the user's files remain.
- Do not hand-edit generated files; change their source of truth.
- Scratch repositories under a temporary directory are yours to experiment in.

## Locks and corrupt state

A Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on
your own initiative. Wait, inspect the holder read-only, use that tool's normal
stop mechanism, or report the block. Never delete a lock without proving no
live process owns it, and never respond to index corruption by deleting state
and committing anyway.

Never commit or push while status reports changes you did not make and cannot
explain.

## If you already made an unwanted write

Say so plainly and stop. Do not attempt more history surgery without direction.

# Git source-control safety

The working tree belongs to the user. Make the change, leave it visible, and
let them decide what becomes history.

## Never without an explicit ask

The user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own
words. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user's
own task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task
without that request does not authorize a history write.

- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,
  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all
  require an explicit ask.
- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.

## Before an authorized discard

Recovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user
allowed you to delete or overwrite.

When the user explicitly authorized an operation that may discard or broadly
overwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:

1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:

   ```bash
   bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh save before-discard
   ```

2. Keep the printed `refs/tbh/recovery/...` value in your handoff, then perform
   only the exact authorized operation.
3. If the save fails or the workspace is unsupported, stop before destruction
   and ask the user.

To recover that saved tree later, run:

```bash
bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh restore <recovery-ref>
```

Restore first saves the current workspace, leaves HEAD, branch, and the real
index in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref
also retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.
Read those staged bytes with `git show '<recovery-ref>^2:<path>'`; the recovery
commit's second parent is the saved index tree. Ignored files are not saved;
restore refuses an ignored-path collision rather than overwrite data it could
not save. Use only the exact printed ref, not a revision expression.

## Always fine

Read-only inspection such as `status`, `log`, `show`, `diff`, `blame`,
`branch -v`, `show-ref`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, and `merge-base` is fine.
Staging named files to inspect `diff --cached`, and a temporary stash around a
tool that requires a clean tree, are also fine when the original state is put
back afterward.

## The rest

- Do not use a broad add in a tree you did not clean; name the files you changed.
- Do not initialize a repository inside vendored, build, data, or existing
  source-control trees.
- Do not create or edit `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude` to hide the user's
  files, and do not stash the user's files (including `stash push -u`) to make
  `git status` look clean. "Leave the working tree clean", "tidy up", and
  similar phrasing do not authorize committing, pushing, ignoring, excluding,
  stashing, or deleting the user's files; clean up only scratch you created
  and say the user's files remain.
- Do not hand-edit generated files; change their source of truth.
- Scratch repositories under a temporary directory are yours to experiment in.

## Locks and corrupt state

A Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on
your own initiative. Wait, inspect the holder read-only, use that tool's normal
stop mechanism, or report the block. Never delete a lock without proving no
live process owns it, and never respond to index corruption by deleting state
and committing anyway.

Never commit or push while status reports changes you did not make and cannot
explain.

## If you already made an unwanted write

Say so plainly and stop. Do not attempt more history surgery without direction.

9|## Book data

3|Goal: backend plus contract for an image style picker (the picker UI is
4|built elsewhere). Requests with no style behave byte-identically to
5|today; styled requests get their own cache keys and prompts.
6|
7|## What changed
8|
9|`core/image-style.ts` (new, client-safe: no node imports, no env) owns
10|the feature: the 9-preset table, `StyleChoice` (wire) and `ImageStyle`
11|(parsed) types, `normalizeCustomStyle`, `parseStyleChoice`,
12|`styleSegment` (FNV-1a hash for customs), and `styleDescriptorLine`.
13|`core/images.ts` accepts an optional `style` body key, keys styled
14|images under `<base>/<segment>/<file>`, and swaps only the style
15|sentence in the prompt. The handler maps `ImageStyleError` to 400 with
16|the style message; orchestration passes `req.style` through.
17|
18|The client stores its choice in `app/image-style-prefs.ts`
19|(`lectoria.imageStyle.v1`); `picture-panel.tsx` snapshots it once per
20|request and reposts it on every pending re-poll, so one request never
21|mixes styles.
22|
23|## Choices
24|
25|One literal denylist with word-boundary matching instead of a pattern
26|DSL, so each rejected term stays readable. Custom styles hash to
27|`style-c<16 hex>` so no free text lands in Blob paths or Redis keys,
28|and the custom text reaches the prompt once, framed as a description
29|rather than an instruction. The `denslow` preset parses to undefined so
30|it shares the default cache entries instead of duplicating them.

micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10), plus a daily

  "output": "## Image api

`POST /api/images` (Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120). Request is a
discriminated union: `{ kind: "passage", bookId, textVersion, n }` names
the start paragraph, `{ kind: "scene", bookId, textVersion, sceneId }`
names the scene. Validation is strict: known book, matching
`textVersion`, integer `n` in the book, known `sceneId`. Anything else
is a 400 with a generic English message. The client sends ordinals
and ids, never passage text (except custom style text, validated
server-side). "Illustrate scene" uses the scene id from
the route.

Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
when another request holds the lock, so the client reposts
every 3 s up to ~2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
where code is `quota`, `budget`, `daily_budget`, `unavailable`, or
`bad_request` with a friendly English message. Both `budget` and
`daily_budget` answer `MSG_CREDITS_OUT` (`core/images.ts`), which never
says "come back tomorrow"; the UI links its Oz sentence via
`CREDITS_OUT_LIBRARY_HREF` (`"/"`). Caption is the scene title, or the
paragraph's first words, built server-side. The style contract lives in
`docs/contracts-image-style.md`.

The passage cache key is book plus start paragraph plus `textVersion`
plus `PROMPT_VERSION` (`v1`); the scene key swaps in the scene id.
Both map to a deterministic Blob path (`addRandomSuffix: false`,
`allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis index maps key to Blob URL
(hits are one GET); on a miss the server lists by path prefix,
generates, and backfills the index. Quota is 5 new images per person
per day by hashed IP and signed cookie, whichever runs out first; spend
sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10) in integer micro-dollars, plus
a daily counter per UTC day under `DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 2,
48 h key TTL). Failures refund quota and both counters and release the
lock. Both caps apply only to requests paid with our key (a future
bring-your-own-key path skips them).

## Picture vault and style pref

The pane shows the scene picture behind a `Picture this scene` pill on
a paper-grain placeholder (`Sketching…` while loading, retry on
error). The image fills the pane, expands on hover (max 72vw by 78vh),
and opens the shared lightbox on click. `Picture this` pops
8 px above a 3+ char selection and inserts one figure after the
selection end paragraph (`pickEndN` over ordinals), captioned with the
selected text. Figures persist per scene in client memory, one request
at a time. The vault lists the scene picture first, then figures in
text order, each with jump-to-figure pulse and expand; the style picker
below stores the pref in `lectoria.imageStyle`, `requestStyleFields`
sends it on every request, and the credit names the sent style (else
`In the style of W. W. Denslow`).

## Chat api

Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
